free_tier.stated: Port forwarding is currently available on our Windows, macOS, and Linux GUI apps for everyone with a paid Proton VPN plan. The plan table marks P2P/BitTorrent as absent from Proton Free and present on VPN Plus. VPN Plus on the 24-month plan: billed at $83.76 for the first 24 months, then renews at $83.88 every 12 months; the 12-month price is unverified: the pricing page rendered here shows only the monthly and 24-month figures.

egress.terms: unverified: no page read states a Proton VPN traffic allowance for the paid tier; the plan table lists features and speeds, not bytes.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: Account web page generates configs; port control is NAT-PMP on the tunnel gateway, not a REST API. Protocols: WireGuard over UDP and TCP, OpenVPN, IKEv2, Stealth (obfuscated) and Smart Protocol. No SOCKS5 proxy is offered. P2P servers (BitTorrent) are included on paid plans.
tooling: natpmpc from libnatpmp, or the official app; WireGuard config from the account page.
chaining: Provides the public endpoint; the loop that keeps the lease alive is a small daemon a user must run beside the service.

limits.value: NAT-PMP mapping expires in 60 seconds and must be looped: natpmpc -a 1 0 udp 60 -g 10.2.0.1, with sleep 45 between calls; closing the terminal terminates the loop
P2P servers only; port forwarding is not compatible with NAT type 2 (moderate NAT)

binding_note: At 1 TiB/month nothing in the pages read states a byte cap, so the thing that fails first is the mapping: a 60-second NAT-PMP lease driven by a loop, on a port the vendor says usually changes when you reconnect. That is a keepalive dependency, not a volume limit.

identity_cost.detail: An account with an email address; the signup page offers Or sign up for free and then a paid plan, with card, PayPal or Google Pay.

reliability_note: The forwarded port expires 60 seconds after the last NAT-PMP renewal; a crashed loop closes the port silently.
confidence_note: Measured would need an account, a natpmpc loop and a byte count. The moving-port sentence comes from the GUI guide, so the stability claim is documented and the byte ceiling is openly unverified.

evidence.proved: Port forwarding is on all paid plans and not on Free; The port number usually changes when you reconnect to VPN.
A WireGuard config can carry NAT-PMP port forwarding; mappings last 60 seconds and must be renewed in a loop; example allocation port 53186 for both UDP and TCP.
Proton Free has no P2P/BitTorrent and connects to servers in 10 countries; VPN Plus carries P2P.
VPN Plus prices: 9.99 EUR per month monthly, 5.32 EUR per month billed at 63.81 EUR for 12 months, 4.49 EUR per month billed at 107.76 EUR for 24 months.

notes: The practical consequence is that ingress works but the endpoint is not addressable across a reconnect without a control loop that rewrites the consumer's config.

extras.wg_detail: A WireGuard configuration file is generated in the account with the port-forwarding toggle baked in: Select a VPN server that supports P2P (double-arrow icon) and generate a WireGuard configuration file. When doing this, ensure that Select VPN options then NAT-PMP (port forwarding) is enabled. Mappings are then made with natpmpc from a user.
